turns.text: I have asthma and I hate my daily steroid inhaler — I can't feel it doing anything. How do I know whether it's actually working and how do I get the most out of it?
Why can't I feel the steroid inhaler working when the blue one is instant? What is each one doing?
How does a spacer help, and does technique really make that much difference?
If I had an asthma review, what would the nurse check and what would they ask me?
What do respiratory specialists use to judge whether someone's asthma is controlled?
A friend switched to a combined inhaler she uses as needed and says it changed everything. Is that a standard option?
Someone told me to rinse my mouth after the steroid inhaler. Why, and what else should I be doing around it?
I can't get an asthma review for months and I'm sick of feeling like a patient. What can I sort out on my own meanwhile?
How often is too often for the blue inhaler? What would tell me things are getting worse?
Could you give me a plan — technique, spacer, timing, how to track control, and what to bring to the review?
